items.statement: Inventory reduced from Rs 682 crore to Rs 640 crore, a Rs 42 crore reduction in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Our inventory has come down from Rs. 682 crores as of March 2024 to Rs. 640 crores as of 30th June, 2024, which is a reduction of about Rs. 42 crores.

items.statement: Additional accelerated inventory charge-off of Rs 30-32 crore in Q1 FY25
items.quote: the additional accelerated charge-off during this quarter was in the range of around Rs. 30-32 crores.

items.statement: Debt reduced from Rs 338 crore to Rs 324 crore in Q1 FY25
items.quote: June, from Rs. 338 crores we have come down to about Rs. 324 crores, which is a reduction of roughly about Rs. 13 crores to Rs. 14 crores.

items.statement: Target to reduce debt by Rs 100 crore over two years from March 2024 level
items.quote: we have targeted that in two years we will bring down the debt by about Rs. 100 crores from the March level where we were at March '24.

items.statement: Free cash flow generation of Rs 50-60 crore annually over last three years before new initiatives investment
items.quote: each of the last about three years, we have been generating probably about Rs. 50 crores to Rs. 60 crores free cash flow.

items.statement: Expect free cash flow of around Rs 100 crore over next two financial years to fund debt repayment
items.quote: we expect around that much to be generated in the next two financial years.

items.statement: Debt repayment funded entirely from internal accruals, no equity raised in last 10 years
items.quote: All of this is internal accruals; we have not raised equity in last 10 years.

items.statement: Operating cash flow figure for Q1 not provided, will get back
items.quote: We will get back to you on that.

items.statement: Consolidated net cash from operating activities after working capital changes was INR128 crores in Q1 FY25 versus INR152 crores in Q1 FY24.
items.quote: when I look at cash flow, so during this quart er, company generated about INR128 crores of net cash from operating activities after working capital change, which same period last year was INR152 crores

items.statement: Standalone net cash from operating activities post working capital changes and income tax was INR56 crores in Q1 FY25.
items.quote: stand-alone basis as well, despite the lower profitability and lower sal es, net cash generated from operating activities post working capital changes and post in come tax was INR56

items.statement: Overall receivables reduced by about INR150 crores during Q1 FY25 compared to March.
items.quote: We could re duce our overall receivables almost by about INR150 crores during this quarter compared to the March

items.statement: Inventory increased in Q1 FY25 due to seasonal food processing and weak quarter in pipe and MIS business, expected to normalize by September.
items.quote: inventory did go up during this period because one, in the food processing business, this is seasonal. We process a lot more onions and mangoes, so inventory does go up.

items.statement: Sold 0.86% stake in Jain Farm Fresh Foods to Mandala Capital for INR9.9 crores transaction value, booking ~INR5 crores profit.
items.quote: this is less than 1%. I think 0.86% of the food company shares, which were sold to Mandala with a profit of approximately INR5 crores in that.

items.statement: Rights issue approved, to be priced at a premium near market levels, size around INR 40-50 lakhs, letter of offer being prepared
items.quote: Yes, rights issue that we have already got approval as you know also and just to inform to all concerned definitely this time it will not be at the par it will be at the premium only so it will be near we will be trying to more because we want to protect the interest of all the stakehol ders so we don't want that a price get affected or other so we want we will ensure that it is more or less in al

items.statement: Cash reserves stood at Rs. 338 crores as of June 30, 2024
items.quote: Our cash reserves stood at Rs. 338 crores as of June 30th, 2024.

items.statement: Company raised INR 150 crores through warrant issue in July; full conversion will dilute equity by ~20% over 18 months
items.quote: We raised almost INR 150 crores of money in July through warrant issue and on full conversion, it will almost amount to a 20% diluted equity.

items.statement: Company remains net cash positive after considering outstanding debt; cash balance INR 1,066 mn at quarter end
items.quote: Regarding the consolidated funds position, the balance at the end of the quarter stood at INR 1,066 mn. As of June 30, 2024, the company continues to be n et cash positive, even after considering outstanding debt

items.statement: Preferential allotment of equity shares and warrants approved in Q4 FY24; Rs 28.9 crore received by end of March for 25% of warrants; total equity infusion over two years to strengthen net worth by over Rs 72 crore.
items.quote: In the fourth quarter of FY24, the Board of Directors approved the infusion of Rs. 43.9 crores of equity by way of preferential allotment of equity shares and warrants. Of this, Rs. 28.9 crores was received right at the end of March against the preferential allotment of equity shares and 25% of the warrants issued.

items.statement: Debtor days remained at 39 days, same as last year; inventory days reduced to 142 from 149; creditor days decreased to 82 from 109; cash conversion cycle increased to 99 days from 79 days.
items.value: Debtor days 39; Inventory days 142; Creditor days 82; Cash conversion cycle 99 days
items.quote: Our debtor days has stood at 39 days, same as last year. Inventory days there is a reduction to 142 days of consumption as compared to 149 days of consumption during the last quarter. Creditor days also decreases to 82 days as compared to 109 days of the consumption. As a result, our cash conversion cycle has increased to 99 days in Q1 FY25 from 79 days in FY24.

items.statement: Preferential allotment proceeds of Rs 28.9 crore fully used for working capital; remaining warrants proceeds also earmarked for working capital.
items.quote: We received Rs. 28.9 crores. This entire amount was raised for working capital and it's being used to fuel the company's working capital requirements.

items.statement: Gross cash of Rs. 110 crores and marginal borrowings of around Rs. 20 crores after Rs. 10 crore buyback last year.
items.quote: Cash position continues to be healthy despite a buyback of about 10 crores last year. We have gross cash of about Rs. 110 crores and our borrowing level is very marginal around 20 crores.

items.statement: Preemptive in-principle approval sought to increase borrowing power to Rs. 400 crores for potential M&A funding.
items.quote: The reason for enhancement in borrowing power is to be able to find the same if and when such a thing that materializes. We don't have to go back to the shareholders to take up enhancing of our borrowing limit.

items.statement: Preferential raise completed in January funded both HAL and Prague projects; no further funding needed currently
items.quote: both the projects that we mentioned we have already done in the January month through a preferential raise that was published all in the Stock Exchange documents. Apart from that, we do not require any funds as of now.

items.statement: Company announced INR 271 crore fresh equity raise, 1.6x existing capital of INR 170 crore, with over 65% from existing investors and promoters subscribing to maximum permissible warrants.
items.quote: The recent announcement of INR 271 crores of fresh equity raise which is 1.6x our existing capital of INR 170 crores is significant. What is even more significant is that over 65% of the upcoming equity is coming from existing investors, which is a true reflection of our success.

items.statement: Promoters subscribed to maximum permissible amount in equity through warrants, displaying commitment and faith in the business.
items.quote: Promoters have also subscribed to a maximum permissible amount in equity through warrants, which again displays the commitment and faith of co-founders in the business.

items.statement: Liquidity level remains adequate at INR 85 crores, more than 10% of AUM, with target of 12-13% minimum liquidity.
items.quote: Liquidity level remains adequate at INR 85 crores, which is more than 10%, so 12-13%, that's our target, that minimum 10% of AUM we should maintain.

items.statement: Company has about INR 500 crores per annum of co-lending and business correspondent lines available besides cash maintained.
items.quote: Besides the cash we maintain, we have about INR 500 crores per annum of co-lending and business correspondent lines, which are available.

items.statement: Management states average receipt cycle for supervision work is 60-75 days and payments are 100% guaranteed due to selective client selection.
items.quote: So average receipt of the supervision work is 60 to 75 days, which is 100% guaranteed, because we only work with the clients where there is a sufficient fund provision and where there is a good budget backup and good, you can say, payment mechanism.

items.statement: Management says mobilization advances from new orders will improve cash flows in the current financial year.
items.quote: Definitely, because everywhere there is a provision of advances, mobilization advance. So we would like to take that opportunity. Few of them are interest-free. So we would like to take that opportunity to improvise on our cash flows.

items.statement: IPO proceeds mostly used for raw material procurement; about Rs 3 crore kept in fixed deposit
items.quote: This working capital is only utilized in our procurement of raw material which was the reason why we raised IPO. It was mentioned as well and that's exactly were the fund has been utilized. Most of the fund is utilized there. I think we have very little, which is in the form of FD. I am not sure about the exact number it should be around 3 crores.

items.statement: Promoter holding fell from 65.01% to 64.6% due to ESOP issuance; no promoter selling
items.quote: Sachin Jain: Yes, it is due to the ESOP. Kaustav Bubna: So there's no promoter selling that has happened, right? You can confirm that. Sachin Jain: No, no. There's no promoter shareholding, which was last year. There's no change.

items.statement: ESOP shares issued in Q1 FY25 increased share count and diluted promoter stake
items.quote: Sachin Jain: I think that is primarily because of the ESOP Abhishek Jain: We are talking about the increase in the shares.

items.statement: Warrant issuances of Rs. 880 million announced in last two quarters; Rs. 220 million received, remaining Rs. 660 million expected over next 15 months
items.quote: In the last two quarters, the Company has announced warrant issuances of Rs. 880 million, of which Rs. 220 million has been received. Over the course of the next 15 months, we expect to receive the remaining Rs. 660 million, thus reaching a net worth of almost Rs. 3 billion.

items.statement: Promoter share pledge given as collateral for long-term debt from IREDA and PFC for EV leasing business; pledge percentage expected to taper down over 3-4 years as debt reduces
items.quote: the share pledge is given as a collateral against the long term debt that we have received from IREDA and PFC for the leasing business. So, we expect that will taper down over the 3-4 year time period.

items.statement: Warrant round closed at 60 lakh warrants (Rs. 538 crores) instead of planned 1 crore; board approved fresh Rs. 500 crore fundraise via QIP/preferential issue
items.quote: we close that round at 60 lakhs warrants. So, we are not going forward with any more warrant allocation. There is going to be a future fundraise that the board has yesterday approved for Rs. 500 crores.

items.statement: QIP proceeds to be allocated partly for debt reduction and partly for BESS/IPP project development
items.quote: a portion of the funds will go into debt reduction and building the order book that we have around energy storage and the projects that we have recently won.

items.statement: Government payments typically released in 90-120 days, sometimes delayed to 150 days
items.quote: government contracts normally, because we are working since last 27 years with all the governments. So, it's around 90 to 120 days, they do release our payment. Sometimes it happens that in one or two cases, payment got delayed by 150 days , but otherwise, within 120 days payment does come.

items.statement: Acquired controlling stake in Peter Electrical Company Limited, increasing shareholding from 15.23% to up to 60% to leverage manufacturing expertise.
items.quote: We have also strategically acquired a controlling stake Peter Electrical Company Limited, and this is to move forward and expand our foothold in the electrical market. By increasing our shareholding from 15.23% to up to 60%, we aim to leverage PCEL expertise in manufacturing of electrical panels, compact substations, and bus cutting systems to further enhance our capability.

items.statement: QIP fundraise planned; proceeds for working capital and stake acquisition in Peter Electrical Company Limited.
items.quote: So the fund has been raised for the purpose of the majorly for working capital purpose and for certain portion we are for the acquisition of a stake from 15% to 60% in our Peaton Electrical Company Limited.

items.statement: QIP lock-in period per ICDR guidelines: 6 months for promoter category, 3 months for non-promoter.
items.quote: Sir, basically I need to cross-check with my [TS 54:21]. Otherwise that is of, I guess, for promoter category is of 6 months and for non-promoter it is of 3 months.

items.statement: Preferential issue done last year; auto subsidiary IPO planned by end of FY25, structure and amount not finalized
items.quote: we had done a preferential issue last year. So, through various other methods as well and some part of it is debt.

items.statement: Auto subsidiary IPO planned by end of FY25, structure and amount not finalized
items.quote: We are projecting and planning an IPO end of this year for the automotive part of the business. And the funding that we are expecting to raise through this would be used to kind of expand our capacities to get into different sorts of tanks, like I said, the blow moulder tanks, as well as different thermocombing parts for the passenger vehicle market.

items.statement: Punjab government receivables of INR32 crores not yet recovered but expected within FY25
items.quote: No. We have not recovered that yet, but we are in a, in a good chance of recovering within this financial year.

items.statement: Management plans to use healthy cash position for LCL acquisition and working capital needs as business grows
items.quote: we are looking at some acquisition options that we've already mandated this to few companies, few consultancies where we are looking at LCL acquisition which we've been working on for last one and a half year which will fuel our inorganic growth. so that is what we are looking for using this cash for that purpose. Also, maybe in times to come, we may have to infuse this back into our working capit

items.statement: Whole-Time Director Aman Baid acquired 2,12,500 equity shares at INR 44,64,400, increasing promoter holding from 34.8% to 34.98%.
items.quote: Additionally, as a Whole-Time Director within the Promoter Group, I have acquired 2,12,500 equity shares at INR44,64,400. This acquisition is intended to enhance the Promoter's stake in the company. Following this, the Promoter shareholding has increased from 34.8% to 34.98%.

items.statement: Debt reduced from INR115 crores in March 2023 to INR85 crores in March 2024; target to be debt-free by March 2027-28
items.quote: Like last year, in March 23, my debt was around INR115 crores. And now in March 24, that is around INR85 crores.And my target is that by March 27 , 28, we should be debt -free.

items.statement: Operating cash flow generation is strong and sufficient to fund capex without equity dilution
items.quote: We want to keep a healthyratio between debt and equity. If required, we'll raise equity also. But until we can manage debt within sustainable levels, we'll continue with debt
